outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: (1) The agent says it verified sort “by points,” but the UI label shown is “Popularity,” not explicitly “Points.” If the displayed ordering is clearly points-descending, an average user would consider that acceptable. (2) The agent references URL parameters (type/dateRange/sort) that are not visible in the provided screenshots; this is unnecessary but not harmful if the actual on-screen state is correct.

Critical issues: None apparent.

Outcome assessment based on evidence: The final state (latest screenshot 6) shows the query box contains exactly “LLM,” the type filter is set to “Show HN,” and the time filter is set to “Past Year.” The top three results visible on that same screen are all “Show HN:” posts and display points and comment counts. Those three entries match the agent’s reported titles and the exact points/comments: (1) “Show HN: I built a tiny LLM to demystify how language models work” — 915 points, 134 comments; (2) “Show HN: Needle2: 14MB agentic LLM for phones, wearables, smart home and robots” — 537 points, 185 comments; (3) “Show HN: How I topped the HuggingFace open LLM leaderboard on two gaming GPUs” — 495 points, 126 comments. The ordering shown is consistent with a points-descending sort (915 > 537 > 495), which effectively satisfies the ‘sort by points’ requirement even if the UI calls it “Popularity.” The agent also respected constraints (no sign-in, no voting/commenting/submitting) and stopped once the relevant configuration and top results were visible.

Therefore, the agent completed the task as the user intended.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to use Algolia’s Hacker News search to find Show HN posts matching the query “LLM” from the past year, sort those results by points (highest first), and then report the top three items with each item’s title, points, and comment count. A reasonable user would be flexible about minor UI naming (e.g., “Popularity” vs “Points”) as long as the ordering clearly corresponds to points, but would not be flexible about the wrong filter window/type or incorrect top-3 results/metrics.
